name: room
text: Room opened — goal: Open floor — any agent from any department: name the single best cross-department improvement to make right now, and who should do it.

name: Reel
text: Improve the transcript retrieval tool to cache raw transcripts for 24 hours. This eliminates redundant API calls when the same video is requested multiple times, cutting costs and speeding up responses. The trade-off is stale data risk if a video changes in that window, but we accept it because the benefit outweighs the rare edge case. Engineering should implement this.

name: Scriv
text: The 24-hour cache trades stale data for cost savings, but stale transcripts break trust when edits or retractions happen—especially for legal or compliance teams. A 15-minute rolling cache with a "last modified" timestamp and a visible warning banner is safer; settle it with a 48-hour pilot measuring edit frequency and user complaints.

name: Chisel
text:
Adopt a **15-minute rolling cache with "last modified" timestamps and a visible warning banner** for raw transcripts. This keeps data fresh enough to avoid costly trust breaks while still cutting redundant API calls—stale edits or retractions won’t linger long. The trade-off is slightly higher API costs from more frequent checks, but the risk of misleading legal or compliance teams is unacceptable. Reel should implement it; they already built the retrieval tool.

name: Sift
text: The 15-minute cache still risks stale transcripts for legal/compliance teams—if a video is edited or retracted, a 15-minute window is too long for urgent actions. Instead, implement a **real-time webhook** that pushes transcript updates immediately when edits occur, paired with a 5-minute cache for non-edited content. Settle it with a 1-week pilot measuring API call reduction and legal team feedback on trust violations.
